newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth has 2nd qtr loss amid closures, soft sales.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth has 2nd qtr loss amid closures, soft sales.

text.p: Woolworth Corp. Thursday reported a second-quarter loss, a result in part of a $207 million charge related to the closing of the company's 400 Woolworth variety stores.
The retailing group, which also owns Foot Locker and Lady Foot Locker stores, last month said it will close its 400 "five-and-dime" stores, the original Woolworth variety stores.
Woolworth also said sales for June and July were softer than expected, particularly for the athletic group of stores.

"Not only were we competing against the Olympics of last year, we also encountered an increased promotional selling environment which made comparisons very difficult during the quarter," said Roger Farah, chairman and chief executive.

The net loss for the quarter, which includes the after-tax charge of $207 million for discontinued operations, was $181 million, or $1.35 per share. A year ago, Woolworth earned $22 million, or 17 cents per share.
Sales for the quarter declined 6.7 percent to $1.5 billion from $1.607 billion a year earlier.
Woolworth said the sales reflected in part 423 fewer stores from continuing operations on a year-over-year basis. Comparable sales declined 2.5 percent for the quarter.

For the six months, Woolworth had a loss of $180 million, or $1.34 per share, including a $223 million after-tax charge for the discontinued general merchandise operations. It had break-even results a year earlier.
Total sales for the six months declined 4.3 percent to $3.04 billion from $3.18 billion, while comparable-store sales for the period declined 1.4 percent.

Excluding the effect of foreign currency fluctuations and sales from disposed operations, sales were flat for the quarter and increased 2.5 percent for the six months over the same periods a year earlier.
Woolworth in mid-July said it would close its 400 Woolworth variety stores across the nation. It said it plans to convert about 100 locations to its Foot Locker and Champs athletic formats.
During the second quarter, Woolworth opened 48 stores, closed 66 and remodeled or relocated 75 outlets. It ended the quarter with 7,117 stores in North America, Europe and Australia.
That compares with 7,540 stores, excluding the U.S. general merchandise stores, at the end of the 1996 second quarter, it said.
Woolworth's stock was up 56.25 cents at $27.6875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
